messages:
Simon: ran a long nsys+perfetto trace on the kv-cache slab workload (small batches, high churn). timeline shows repeated cudaMalloc spikes aligned with arena reclaim windows. attaching the key snippets below — please read before morning stand :eyes:

perf-bot: nsys capture finished: https://perf.internal/trace/2023456789 (capture size 1.3GB) :white_check_mark:

Alex: ok can you paste the hotspot lines? curious if it's cudaMalloc or ffi allocation path

Simon: tl;dr: heap churn -> cudamalloc path dominates host time at the edges. p95 gen latency up ~12% and throughput down ~7% on the microbenchmark when the kv cache reaches eviction pressure.

Simon: perfetto slice (condensed):
```
[ 0.000s ] kernel: inference_step  (30 ms)
[ 0.030s ] nvtx: kvcache:evict_prefix
[ 0.031s ] cudaFree / cudaMalloc (sync)  (7.2 ms)
[ 0.038s ] kernel: small_attention (2.8 ms)
[ 0.041s ] malloc-host  (sync) (1.1 ms)
[ 0.042s ] kernel: matmul_fused  (40 ms)
[ 0.082s ] cudaMalloc (sync) (8.1 ms)
// repeating pattern every ~100-220ms during batch storm
```

Maya: that pattern smells like arena fragmentation + thread contention on the pool. are we on cudamallocAsync or fallback?

Simon: allocator config we used for the run:
```
allocator.arena_size = 256MB
allocator.slab_size = 2MB
allocator.reclaim_threshold = 0.60
allocator.max_small_alloc = 128KB
use_cudapool_v2 = false
use_cudamalloc_async = false
```

Jordan: aha, reclaim_threshold 0.60 is low. when eviction spikes we scatter free lists and a bunch of small allocations fall back to cudaMalloc. fragmentation + thundering herd.

Alex: do we have a flame or stack sample showing callsites?

Simon: sampled stacks (top callers):
```
kv_cache_alloc(void*)
-> slab_alloc
-> arena_alloc
-> allocator_try_fastpath
-> cudaMalloc
```
counts: cudaMalloc ~420 calls in 60s window during the storm, baseline ~8 calls.

Maya: can we reproduce with pool enabled? maybe cudamallocAsync reduces sync stalls. Also consider increasing slab_size or enabling consolidation to coalesce small frees.

Simon: tried quick experiment: enabling use_cudapool_v2 reduced cudaMalloc calls to ~18 in same window and p95 regained most of the lost latency. but we saw a different issue: kernel selector started emitting different kernel variants for matmul depending on available workspace -> different workspace sizes caused allocation size oscillation.

Jordan: that's interesting — selector thrash could be because workspace allocator returns slightly different alignment/size, so selector heuristics pick a different kernel each time. that causes cache misses + kernel cold paths.

Alex: any logs showing kernel name churn?

Simon: yes excerpt from timeline (kernel names):
```
matmul_algo=wino128_workspace=48MB
matmul_algo=gemm_tiled_workspace=24MB
matmul_algo=wino128_workspace=48MB
matmul_algo=gemm_tiled_workspace=24MB
```
This alternates with the allocation spikes.

Maya: two-pronged fix request: 1) stabilize allocator so workspace sizes are deterministic (pad to slab boundaries, deterministic alignment), 2) change selector fallback to prefer stable kernels when variance small.

Simon: tried padding allocs to 2MB boundary (slab_size) in a local build — kernel churn stopped, cudaMalloc calls dropped further, p95 improved another 4%.

Jordan: action items I propose: 
- nightly canary: enable use_cudapool_v2 + slab_padding=2MB for 24h 
- update selector: add a stability_penalty to kernel scoring to avoid switching for <10% perf delta
- monitoring: add nvtx marker in kv-cache reclaim path and alert if cudaMalloc calls per-min > 50

Alex: sounds good. also add a feature-flag fallback that forces legacy pooling if we detect fragmentation increase on Dedicated clusters.

Maya: I'll own the canary and the alert. Simon can you push the slab_padding branch + perf traces to the canary?

Simon: will do. pushing traces and config to infra canary in ~30m. leaving trace links in the ticket.

perf-bot: ticket created: INF-8764 "kv-cache: slab jitter -> allocator padding + selector stability" assigned to Maya/Simon/Jordan :spiral_note_pad: 

Simon: thanks everyone, I'll drop the minimal repro + perf script into the ticket. :thumbsup:
